sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's coal-heavy grid and rising power demand make geothermal and gas-transition capacity from BREN and PGEO a durable earnings driver regardless of global sentiment.
Jakarta's EV supply-chain push, including nickel downstreaming and battery adoption, underpins VKTR's structural growth even as global EV sentiment swings.
Corporate and sovereign net-zero mandates are steadily expanding offtake for Indonesian renewables, giving POWR and TPIA long-duration contracted cash flows that smooth cyclical drawdowns.
sectors.ai: Renewables are underperforming on both sides of the Pacific, so treat this as a WATCH, not a buy. Rotate selectively into BREN and VKTR on strength, keep PGEO as a lower-beta hold, and avoid adding to the broader basket until the aggregate signal turns from WATCH to accumulate.

Brand consolidation and distribution expansion into tier-2 and tier-3 cities remain the durable earnings driver for local consumer companies, independent of US FMCG sentiment.

Avoid US-facing FMCG exposure, which is dragging the composite. Treat the NORMAL signal as permission to trade, not to hold passively.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's archipelago geography and fragmented inter-island shipping make efficient logistics infrastructure a durable, decades-long structural requirement tied to domestic consumption growth.
E-commerce penetration in Indonesia continues to expand faster than warehousing and last-mile capacity, sustaining long-term demand for cold chain, fulfilment, and urban delivery networks.
Rising fuel, labour, and fleet-renewal costs are forcing consolidation toward scaled operators with pricing power, making cost efficiency a durable competitive moat in Indonesian logistics.
sectors.ai: Logistics is a WATCH, not a buy: aggregate weakness (-0.80%) with gains concentrated in micro-caps (TRUK +9.65%, MITI +5.04%, SOCI +4.03%) signals speculative rotation, not sector recovery. Indonesia's -0.84% underperformance versus US -0.62% reflects soft domestic freight demand and rupiah pressure on imported fuel and fleet costs. Avoid chasing TRUK and MITI; instead accumulate quality names on weakness, and wait for volume confirmation in mid-caps like BESS and GTRA before adding exposure.
